about: PLACEHOLDER (docs/PLACEHOLDERS.md): Which prop art (manifest.json in this folder) dresses each thing in data/locations, read by world/look/set_dressing.gd (docs/art/set_dressing.md). A location prop or container is looked up by its id in `ids` first, then by its `model` in `models`; with neither it uses the art of the same name as its model, else `container_default` for containers. A value is an art id, or {art, mount, scale} to override how it hangs (`big`: it keeps its real size in a tight spot, as a building-sized piece does; the horses), or null for an invisible spot (something already drawn, or a view). `on_wall` is the art used when the thing stands on a wall square (shelves against a wall). Doors take the first `doors.rules` entry whose words are in their id or label. `floors` gives a place its own ground texture; `low_cover.<place>` and `<place>_run` dress its '=' squares. An entry with `building: true` stands in for the whole house on its square (a windmill, a bell tower) and, like the houses, opens a window round the party where it hides it (SeeThrough); `see_through: true` does the same for a tall piece of stone or timber (a colossus, a hut), and `fade: true` fades a tall piece like the trees instead. `scales` sizes a piece wherever it stands (stairs fill their square); `fronts` gives furniture a front view that stands flat against a wall beside it. `rooms` gives a location's areas their own floor and wall by words in the area's name (a bathroom's tiles); `place_looks` overrides a whole place's floor, wall, difficult ground and `rock_walls` (cliffs instead of trees) and, beside it, `tree_walls` (rectangles [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] of wall squares drawn as trees all the same in the Modern look: a mountain's wooded lower slopes under its bare crags). `feet` is each standing piece's real height (a person is 6 ft; 1 unit = 5 ft): the piece is drawn at that size, and `feet` is the height of its picture at real size (low, deep things such as beds include the top you see from above). A piece wider than `big_width` units at that size (a cottage, a tent, a wagon) keeps its size whatever the room and clears the trees and the board's own scenery around it. `glows` are pieces drawn unshaded, giving light rather than taking it. `double_doors` are exit art drawn once across a doorway two squares wide (outside interiors: the keep's great doors). `rooms` applies to interiors and dungeons only; `outdoor_rooms` are the few rules for outdoor maps (jetties are planks). `runs_along` lists long, thin pieces (a fence) that lie along a run of low cover going up the map instead of facing south. `map_marks` draws a building-sized 3D piece on the minimap over the squares it stands on (fill, rim, stripes of its canvas, round or square, at `scale` of its footprint). `theme_rooms` are a board theme's own room styles, checked first (a farmhouse bedroom is plaster and planks); a place_looks entry with `keep` keeps its look in every room (a cave, the Amber Temple). Room words match an area's name before its id. `low_cover_rooms` dress a room's '=' squares by words in its name (`single`, `run`, `wall_run`), unless the place has its own set. `furnish` fills rooms out with what a room of its kind holds (world/look/furnish.gd).

models3d.about: 3D pieces from art/models (blender/models_3d.py, docs/art/models.md) that stand in for 2D art, by art id; a value can be {board theme: model, "*": model} (wooden stairs indoors, stone ones elsewhere) or a list of variants the board picks from by square (pines, boulders). Only the places listed use them ("*": everywhere, owner sign-off 2026-10-06). walls: a wall surface whose painted panelling gets 3D panels on every open face.

building_kit.about: Town houses from the building kit (art/models/kit, blender/building_kit.py, docs/art/building_kit.md): the style each place's houses are built in (its own, else its board theme's); a place or theme not named keeps the plain boxes. The house that holds a church's doors is built in the church style (stone, buttresses, lancets and a bell tower). cores: the house's wall behind the modules (a texture set, or none for a dark core where boards cover it). roofs: thatch or slate for small houses and for grand ones (grand_area squares or more). paints: the colours Vallaki's clapboard houses are painted, one per house. cut_away: whether a town house or Castle Ravenloft's walls cut down when they stand between the camera and the party (off: owner 2026-10-13); off, they stand and open a window round the party (SeeThrough).

bend.about: Natural shapes for buildings (natural maps B1, owner 2026-10-19: "We can give buildings natural shapes instead of their straight lines"; BuildingBend, docs/art/building_kit.md): a building's points are moved once when it is built, so its walls lean and bow, its corners drift, a timber house's upper storey juts, the ridge sags and the eaves wave: a wall never more than its style's reach sideways (a quarter of a square, half for timber walls: Ashwin's pick, 2026-10-19), a roof (overhead) a quarter square further at its ridge. reach: how far a style's walls may go, in squares (default 0.25). styles: how far each style bends, 1 the most (a Barovian timber cottage); places: a place's own amount over its style's (Castle Ravenloft's outer yards stay as raised by power, the Abbey and Argynvostholt are old and tired); overhang: how far a style's upper storey juts out at full amount. A town's yard walls and palisade take the style's amount too. The Classic look never bends.

interiors.about: Interiors: the style a place's rooms are built in, by the start of its id, else by board theme. A lone wall square inside a room is a pillar in that style (kit_pillar_<style>); every open face of a cut-away wall gets the style's coping along its top and, where no panelling does, its face module (kit_<style>_coping, kit_<style>_face). full_walls (W8, Modern look only): rooms get full-height walls, height by style, which open a window round the party where they hide it (SeeThrough); cut_away: they drop to the cut-away height toward the camera instead (off: owner 2026-10-17, "walls collapse down when looking from certain angles"); thin_walls (Natural Maps Plan I1, owner 2026-10-19): the side of a wall that faces a room is set back into the wall square by inset (0.35 of a square), so a wall between two rooms stands a foot and a half thick, not a whole square, and the places named in not (starts of ids: the caves, which have their own walls) keep whole squares; ground: what lies outside the building by style, and outside: a place's own (its ground, how many storeys below it lies, its walls' height); a dungeon's outside is rock. An iron style (the Ghostlight Express's Tender) has no face or coping modules: its walls are the plain riveted plate of their own surface.

castle.about: Castle Ravenloft from outside (W19, CastleBuilder, Modern look only), by place: rect is the castle's part of the map [x, z, w, d] (its wall squares are the castle; walls outside it stay as they were); wall and keep are the curtain walls' and the keep's heights; keeps are rects of keep squares; blocks are more of the castle past the map's edge [x, z, w, d, height]; towers are round towers {at: [x, z] in squares, r, h, from (above 0 a turret rising out of the keep, below 0 a tower rising out of the drop), spire: cone, needle or none}; parapets are rects whose wall squares are a low wall (the cliff road's edge); heights are rects [x, z, w, d, height] of walls of their own height (a raised roof's parapet); cliffs false makes the void a drop off the castle's roofs, its masonry going down `below` under every square beside it instead of rock; bridges are rects of the squares that span the chasm (timbers under them, no cliffs); walks true makes the place's built raised squares (raised floor digits with elevation stacked on them) the wall walk and its stairs, in the castle's stone (W7).

clutter.about: Decals laid over floors and walls by rule (world/look/clutter.gd, docs/art/decals.md): per board theme, or per place by the start of its id. decals: decal ids or sheet names (art/textures/decals/manifest.json); on: floor, edge (beside a wall), difficult, boundary (beside rough ground: mud fringes where cobbles meet mud), wall or wall_foot (an open face of a wall); chance per square; size in world units; max per board; tint darkens or colours a mark; gloss makes it wet (puddles glint). A rule with scatter instead names kit models (blender/building_kit.py kit_scatter_*) strewn on the ground the same way. rooms: words in an area's name or id that a rule is kept to (straw only in a stable).

hand_placed.about: Things placed by hand (Natural Maps Plan I3, interiors, Modern look only). loose: the pieces a person sets down rather than lines up (a barrel, a crate, a chair, a basket, a stack of books): each stands off its square's middle by between half of `shift` of a square and all of it, and turned by between half of `turn` degrees and all of it, seeded by the square and never out of it. Pieces people line up (pews, beds, shelves, wardrobes, counters, tables against a wall) are not listed and keep their lines. one_piece: a straight run of three or more low-cover squares of one of these (a long table) is built as one long piece, its ends as modelled and its middle stretched, instead of a row of short ones; a run with something of the location's on it stays a row.

furnish.about: Lived-in rooms (world/look/furnish.gd, docs/art/interiors.md): what a room of its kind holds, besides the things its location names. rooms: [[words in the area's name, else its id], {wall, floor, centre: [art], rug: surface}], first match; themes: the board theme's set where no room matches. A wall piece goes on about `wall_fill` of the free wall faces, a floor piece on about `floor_fill` of the free squares along a wall (never in a passage one square wide), a low thing on about `centre_fill` of the open floor (never two side by side), a rug under the middle of a room whose rule names one; never beside doors, exits, spawns, lights or people, nor on a wall square holding the location's own things. Pieces in `lit` (lanterns, candles) give a little light, at most `lights_per_room` in a room. sets: named sets an area picks with `furnish: "<set>"` instead of its kind (a burned hall's debris); a rule or set may give its own wall_fill, floor_fill and centre_fill.

theme_rooms.about: Room styles for one board theme, checked before the general `rooms`: a farmhouse's bedrooms are plaster and planks, not a manor's carpet and wallpaper. A dungeon's halls, galleries and chambers stay stone (the Region Variety Plan: the dragon's gallery was laid in checker marble).
